paper.title: MEMRES: A Memory-Augmented Resolver with Confidence Cascade for Agentic Python Dependency Resolution
paper.central_claim: A six-level confidence cascade (session memory, curated compatibility maps/templates, co-occurrence mining, heuristics, then LLM last) with intra-session memory, self-evolving memory (tips/shortcuts), an error-pattern KB, semantic import analysis and Python 2 detection resolves 86.6% (10-run avg) of HG2.9K snippets with Gemma-2 9B vs PLLM's reported 54.7%, with 68.0% resolved without any LLM call.

provenance.notes: Opus aggregate seat via the configured claude-kimi type fable; no route probing. actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref are null because the subagent runtime exposes no verifiable provider receipt to this worker.

rs_pattern.reason: Opus: the central operation is 'only call the LLM when all deterministic rules fail'. Each sub-problem goes to an exact handler or the pip/Docker resolver, and the LLM emits constrained version pins checked by build, which is C25 (son55). The failure-category partition (Python 2 syntax / name mismatch / version / C-extension) with tailored treatments is a real secondary move (sol's heterogeneous_decomposition; sub null, since C04 is about compressing trained artifacts). sol's adapt_via_conditioning is dropped: exact reuse is a cache, and partial-match 'hints' do not condition a model's task generalization.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On HG2.9K with Gemma-2 9B, the full cascade resolves 86.6% (10-run mean) and a within-batch, Docker-validated memory adds about 5 pp over the same pipeline without it; efficiency is much better than PLLM's published figures.
assessment.author_claim_vs_supported: Superiority over PLLM and attribution to the confidence cascade/self-evolving memory are not isolated: baseline is a copied number and almost all components are unablated.
unresolved: Opus: the text's 'disabling Level 1 only increases runtime' contradicts Table 2 (opus:O01, opus:O02).
Opus: the measured retained effect is a near-duplicate solution cache on the evaluated batch (opus:O03).
assessment.note: retained scoped to the Level 1 store-off ablation inside a single batch; no improver-level or cross-run retention; headline gain is mostly static curated knowledge.
assessment.evidence_level_note: Both seats retained, kept and scoped. A Docker-gated store written during the batch is read on later, different snippets, and the same-pipeline Level 1 OFF arm loses 5.0 pp. Run precedent (r06a SWE-Exp, r15b Evo-MedAgent) admits same-stream store-off evidence as retained. Its weaknesses (cache of near-duplicate forks, built from the test stream, contradicted by the authors' own text, no ablation variance) are scored in E.causality and E.holdout, not by lowering the level.

G.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. The limitation of the nearest system (PLLM 54.7%, deterministic root causes, wasted LLM time) is concrete and quantified. But the failure analysis is on the evaluation benchmark, the harness-level learning component (memory) is motivated only by PLLM's sequential evaluation, and V2/Repo2Run are named, not compared.

M.reason: Opus sides with son55. The cascade ordering (exact levels first, LLM last, Docker verification) is coherent for the stated root causes. The mechanism behind the headline gain, however, is static curated knowledge, and the self-evolving part is thin: the roles of tips and anti-patterns are unspecified, nothing argues why memory beats a cache, and the authors' own causal account of Level 1 contradicts their ablation (opus:O01). No distinguishing predictions against simpler alternatives are made. sol's 3 credits the cascade's clarity, which X already rewards.

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Levels, Jaccard 0.5, Docker validation, run-level reset and sandboxing are stated. Tip content and use, anti-pattern consumption, KB self-learning conflicts, in-batch expiry or rollback, and the prompt text are missing.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. The full 2890 denominator is used and runtime passes count as failures. But success is import-level only, and the PLLM figure is copied without confirming the same implementation, timeout or LLM.

E.causality.reason: Opus sides with son55. Only Level 1 is tabulated (a near-duplicate cache, opus:O03), and the authors' text contradicts that row (opus:O01). Co-occurrence removal appears only in prose. The 31.9-pp gain over a copied PLLM number is not decomposed: KB, Python 2 detector, semantic analyzer and cascade-vs-LLM-first are all untested (opus:O05). Tips, shortcuts and runtime KB learning are not separated, and there is no same-LLM rerun baseline. Not 0: the store-off row does isolate one retained component.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Mitigations are disclosed: about 50 KB entries come from a disjoint development subset, co-occurrence data is pre-2020, state resets between runs, and no HG2.9K result was used for KB entries. Against that, the design is motivated by failure analysis on the evaluation benchmark (including the Python 2 rule), the store is built from the evaluated batch, and only one dataset and one LLM are used. Not lowered to 1: the test-informed part is a generic rule family rather than instance-level tuning, and no oracle signal enters the loop.

E.statistics.reason: Opus sides with sol (A2 ladder). Ten randomized-order runs with SD (±9.3 snippets) and full failure counts go beyond rung 1. There is no interval or significance test, the comparator is a single published value, and the ablation has no run count or variance, so rung 3 (seeds + intervals + test) is not reached. This matches r07a/r08a (cross-run SD, no CI or test → 2).

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with sol. LLM calls per snippet, the no-LLM share, median and P90 latency and hardware are reported. Latency is success-conditioned (opus:O04), the PLLM comparison uses that paper's figures on other hardware, and failed or retried builds and curation effort are not costed. That is a key fairness gap, not a near-complete ledger.
